parent: 分別禪波羅蜜前方便第六之二

zh: 第四、明證止者，有二解不同：有師云：「止無別證，但能為諸禪作前方便。若有所證，即屬餘禪。」此義至下明善根發中，即是其事。二者、有師言：「止非但通發諸禪，亦自有別證之法，即是五輪禪。所以者何？諸餘法門悉別有安心修習之法，然後次第發禪不同。」今明此止，但制心一處，則五輪自發。譬如淨水無波，則萬像悉現，止亦如是。今明因止證五輪。五輪者：一、地輪；二、水輪；三、風輪；四、金沙輪；五、金剛輪。此五法門，悉是借譬立名。通名為輪者，轉也。如世輪若轉，離此至彼。禪中明輪亦爾，如地輪因離下地亂心，轉至上地，故名為輪。乃至金剛輪義亦復如是，轉至無學極果故。
en: Fourth, clarifying the verification of stopping: there are two differing interpretations here. One master says: "Stopping has no distinct realization of its own — it can only serve as the preliminary expedient means for the other dhyānas. If there is any realization at all, it belongs properly to one of those other dhyānas." This point will be treated further below, exactly where the arising of wholesome roots is clarified. A second master says: "Stopping not only generally brings forth every dhyāna in common, but also has its own distinct method of realization — namely, the five-wheel dhyāna. Why is this? Every other dharma-gate has its own distinct method of settling and cultivating the mind, and only afterward brings forth dhyāna in its own particular sequence." Here, it is clarified that this stopping alone, simply by restraining the mind to a single place, brings forth the five wheels of itself — just as, when clear water is free of ripples, the ten thousand reflections all appear within it of themselves; stopping is exactly the same.

Here, then, the five wheels realized through stopping are clarified. The five wheels are: the earth wheel; the water wheel; the wind wheel; the golden-sand wheel; and the vajra wheel. Each of these five names is borrowed as a comparison to establish its name. They are called, in general, "wheels" because a wheel turns — just as a worldly wheel, once turning, moves from one place to another. The wheels clarified within dhyāna are exactly the same: the earth wheel, for instance, is so named because it turns the scattered mind of the lower stage away and moves it to a higher stage. This holds, in the same way, all the way up to the vajra wheel, which turns one all the way to the ultimate fruit of no-more-learning.

zh: 一、地輪者，如地有二義：一者、住持不動；二者、出生萬物。行者因止若證未到地定，忽然湛心，自覺身心相空，泯然入定，定法持心不動，故名住持。因未到地出生初禪種種功德，事同出生萬物。二、水輪者，水有二義：一、潤漬生長；二、體性柔軟。行者於地輪中若證水輪三昧，即是發諸禪種種功德，定水潤心，自覺心中善根增長，即是潤漬義。因得定故，身心濡軟，折伏高心，心隨善法，即是柔軟義，故名水輪。
en: First, the earth wheel: earth has two properties — first, sustaining and remaining unmoved; second, giving birth to the ten thousand things. If a practitioner, through stopping, realizes the concentration of the "not-yet-arrived" state, the mind suddenly becomes deep and still, and one becomes aware of oneself that the mark of body and mind is empty, dissolving away into concentration; the dharma of concentration itself then sustains the mind unmoved — hence it is called sustaining. And because the "not-yet-arrived" state gives rise to the various merits of the first dhyāna, this matches the property of giving birth to the ten thousand things.

Second, the water wheel: water has two properties — first, moistening and nurturing growth; second, being soft and pliant in its own nature. If the practitioner, within the earth wheel, realizes the samādhi of the water wheel, the various merits of dhyāna are thereby brought forth: the water of concentration moistens the mind, and one becomes aware of oneself that wholesome roots are growing within the mind — this is the meaning of moistening. And because concentration is attained, body and mind become soft and pliant, arrogance is subdued, and the mind comes to follow wholesome dharmas — this is the meaning of softness; hence it is called the water wheel.

zh: 三、風輪者，如世間風，有三義：一者、遊空無礙；二者、鼓動萬物；三者、能破壞。行者發風輪三昧亦如是，若因禪定發相似智慧，無礙方便，如風遊空，一切無礙。鼓動者，得方便道，即能擊發種種出世善根，功德生長。破壞者，智慧方便能摧破一切諸見煩惱。若二乘人得此風輪三昧，即是五方便相似無漏解發。若是菩薩，即入鐵輪十信，是名風輪。四、金沙輪者，金則譬真，沙諭無著。行者若發見思真慧，無染無著，得三道果。若是菩薩，即入三賢十地位中，能破一切塵沙煩惱，是名金沙輪。五、金剛輪者，第九無礙道，名金剛輪三昧。譬如金剛，體堅用利，能摧碎諸物。金剛三昧亦復如是，不為妄惑所侵，能斷一切結使，成阿羅漢。若在菩薩心，即是金剛般若，破無明細惑，證一切種智，亦名清淨禪。菩薩依是禪故，得大菩提果。
en: Third, the wind wheel: worldly wind has three properties — first, traveling through open space without obstruction; second, stirring the ten thousand things; third, being able to destroy. When the practitioner brings forth the samādhi of the wind wheel, it is exactly the same: if, through dhyāna-concentration, an approximate wisdom and unobstructed skillful means are brought forth, this is like wind traveling through open space, unobstructed in every direction. As for stirring: having attained the path of skillful means, one is able to strike and rouse forth every kind of world-transcending wholesome root, and merit grows accordingly. As for destroying: skillful wisdom is able to crush and destroy every wrong view and affliction. If a follower of the two lesser vehicles attains this samādhi of the wind wheel, this is precisely the arising of an approximate, uncontaminated understanding through the five expedient means. If it is a bodhisattva, this is precisely entering the iron wheel of the ten stages of faith. This is called the wind wheel.

Fourth, the golden-sand wheel: gold here serves as a metaphor for truth, and sand serves as a metaphor for non-attachment. If the practitioner brings forth the true wisdom regarding the views and the discursive afflictions, undefiled and unattached, the fruits of the three paths are attained. If it is a bodhisattva, this is precisely entering the stages of the three levels of worthies and the ten grounds, able to break through every affliction as countless as sand and dust. This is called the golden-sand wheel.

Fifth, the vajra wheel: the ninth unobstructed path is called the vajra-wheel samādhi. Just as vajra, being hard in its very substance and sharp in its function, is able to crush and shatter every other thing, the vajra samādhi is exactly the same: undisturbed by any deluded confusion, it is able to sever every fetter, and thereby accomplishes arhatship. Within a bodhisattva's mind, this is precisely the vajra-like prajñā that breaks through the subtle delusion of ignorance and realizes the wisdom that knows all things in every mode — also called the pure-and-undefiled dhyāna. In dependence on this dhyāna, the bodhisattva attains the fruit of great bodhi.

zh: 復次，如輪若無牛御，終不自轉。五輪禪定亦復如是。雖當地各有諸妙功德，若不體真為導，無著熏修，則於地地有礙，便乖輪用。今行者善修體真，無著故，能從初心轉至極果，輪用乃成。是以《法華經》云：「眾生處處著，引之令得出。」當知行者善修止門，則能具足五輪禪定，證三乘聖果。
en: Furthermore: just as a wheel, without an ox to drive it, will never turn on its own, the dhyāna-concentration of the five wheels is exactly the same. Although each stage possesses its own wondrous merits, if embodying-truth stopping is not taken as the guide, and cultivation is not carried out free of attachment, then obstruction arises at every single stage, and the wheel's own function fails. Here, because the practitioner skillfully cultivates embodying-truth stopping, free of attachment, they are able to turn from the very first mind all the way to the ultimate fruit, and the wheel's function is thereby accomplished. Hence the Lotus Sūtra says: "Sentient beings are attached everywhere they turn; I lead them so that they may find their way out." One should know, then, that a practitioner who skillfully cultivates the gate of stopping is thereby able to be complete in the dhyāna-concentration of the five wheels, and realize the noble fruits of all three vehicles.

The five wheels trace a single continuous path from the very threshold of concentration (the earth wheel's "not-yet-arrived" state) to arhatship and beyond into the bodhisattva grounds, each wheel's name unpacked through a genuine property of its physical namesake — earth's stability and fertility, water's moistening and softness, wind's unobstructed reach and its power to stir and to destroy. The closing image is the passage's real punchline: five wheels, however wonderful individually, are inert without an ox to pull them — and embodying-truth stopping, the very practice this whole section has been about, is that ox. Depth of insight into emptiness is what actually keeps the practitioner moving from one stage to the next rather than becoming stuck admiring the merits of wherever they currently stand. This closes the fourth and final part of the gate of stopping, and with it, the whole of 止門 — the first of the internal expedient means' five layers.

zh: 第二、明驗善惡根性者，行人既能善修止門，息諸亂想，則其心澄靜；以心靜故，宿世善根自然開發。若無善者，則發諸惡法。故經云：「先以定動，後以智拔。」止為初門，善、惡二事之中，必有其一，行者應當明識其相，取捨之間不乖正道，故須分別。今就善、惡根性中，即為二意：一、明驗善根性；二、明驗惡根性。然論善惡發之前後，各逐其人，未必定前善而後惡也。
en: Second, clarifying how to verify wholesome and unwholesome capacity: once a practitioner has properly cultivated the gate of stopping and brought every scattered thought to rest, the mind becomes clear and still; and because the mind is still, wholesome roots from past lives naturally come to be brought forth of themselves. Where there is nothing wholesome present, unwholesome dharmas are instead brought forth. Hence the sūtra says: "First stir it through concentration, then draw it out through wisdom."

Since stopping serves as the first gate, one or the other of these two things — the wholesome or the unwholesome — is bound to occur, and the practitioner must clearly recognize its mark, so that nothing goes against the correct path in taking up and setting aside; hence this distinction must be made. Here, within the topic of wholesome and unwholesome capacity, there are two parts: clarifying how to verify wholesome capacity, and clarifying how to verify unwholesome capacity. As for the actual order in which the wholesome and the unwholesome arise, however, this follows each individual practitioner — it is not necessarily fixed that the wholesome always arises first and the unwholesome only afterward.

zh: 第一、明驗善根性，即為四意：一、列善法章門；二、正明善根發相；三、驗知虛實；四、料揀發禪不定。
en: First, clarifying how to verify wholesome capacity: this itself has four parts — first, listing the topics of the wholesome dharmas; second, directly clarifying the marks of wholesome roots arising; third, verifying whether they are genuine or false; fourth, distinguishing that the arising of dhyāna through this is not fixed.

items.en: Listing the Topics of the Wholesome Dharmas

zh: 第一、列善法章門者，善有二種：一者、外善；二者、內善。今就明外善中，善乃眾多，略出五種：一、布施；二、持戒；三、孝順父母師長；四、信敬三寶，精勤供養；五、讀誦聽學。略以此等五種善根，示表外善發相不同。所以悉屬外善者，原其本行悉是散心中修習，未能出離欲界，發諸禪定無漏，故說為外善。
en: First, listing the topics of the wholesome dharmas: the wholesome is of two kinds — external wholesomeness, and internal wholesomeness. Here, within external wholesomeness, the wholesome is manifold; in brief, five kinds are given: giving; upholding the precepts; filial devotion to parents and teachers; faith and reverence toward the Triple Gem, together with diligent offering; and reading, reciting, listening to, and studying the teachings. These five wholesome roots, in brief, serve to indicate the different marks by which external wholesomeness arises. The reason all five are classed as external wholesomeness is that their original practice is, in every case, cultivated within a scattered mind, not yet able to leave the desire realm behind or bring forth the various dhyāna-concentrations and the uncontaminated — hence they are called external wholesomeness.

zh: 二、明內善者，即是五門禪：一、阿那波那門；二、不淨觀門；三、慈心門；四、因緣門；五、念佛三昧門。此五法門通攝一切諸禪，發諸無漏，故名為內善。
en: Second, clarifying internal wholesomeness: this is precisely the five-gate dhyāna — the gate of mindfulness of the breath; the gate of the contemplation of impurity; the gate of loving-kindness; the gate of causation; and the gate of the buddha-recollection samādhi. These five dharma-gates, taken together, encompass every dhyāna, and bring forth every uncontaminated attainment — hence they are called internal wholesomeness.

zh: 問曰：內善無量，何得但說五門？答曰：五名雖少，而行通諸禪。所以者何？一、阿那波那門者，此通至根本及特勝、通明等諸禪三昧；二、不淨觀門者，此通九想、背捨、超越等諸禪三昧；三、慈心門者，此通四無量等諸禪三昧；四、因緣門者，此通至十二因緣、四諦等慧行諸禪三昧；五、念佛門者，此通至九種禪及百八三昧。
en: Question: internal wholesomeness is measureless — how can only five gates be spoken of? Answer: though the five names are few, the practice behind them extends through every dhyāna. Why is this? The gate of mindfulness of the breath extends all the way to the root dhyānas, the sixteen special excellences, the thorough-and-bright contemplation, and other such dhyāna-samādhis. The gate of the contemplation of impurity extends to the nine contemplations, the liberations, the transcendence samādhi, and other such dhyāna-samādhis. The gate of loving-kindness extends to the four immeasurable minds and other such dhyāna-samādhis. The gate of causation extends all the way to the twelve links of dependent origination, the Four Noble Truths, and the other wisdom-conduct dhyāna-samādhis. The gate of buddha-recollection extends all the way to the nine kinds of great dhyāna and the one hundred eight samādhis.

zh: 復次，初數息門，即是世間凡夫禪；次不淨門，即是出世間禪，諸聲聞人所行；次慈心門，即是凡聖二人為大福德修慈，入四無量心；次因緣門者，即是辟支佛人之所行；次念佛門，功德廣大，即是諸菩薩之所行。此則略明五門次第淺深之相。
en: Furthermore: the first, the gate of counting the breath, is precisely the worldly dhyāna of the ordinary person; next, the gate of impurity is precisely a world-transcending dhyāna, practiced by śrāvakas; next, the gate of loving-kindness is precisely what both ordinary people and the noble cultivate together, for the sake of great merit, entering the four immeasurable minds; next, the gate of causation is precisely what is practiced by pratyekabuddhas; and next, the gate of buddha-recollection, whose merit is vast and expansive, is precisely what is practiced by bodhisattvas. This, in brief, clarifies the shallow-to-deep sequence and marks of the five gates.

zh: 復次，五門禪定對治四分煩惱，四分煩惱出生八萬四千塵勞，當知五門亦能出八萬四千法門。此而言之，但說五門，則攝一切內善具足。數人所明初賢五停心觀發，與此有相開處。
en: Furthermore: the dhyāna-concentration of the five gates serves as the antidote to the four divisions of affliction, and the four divisions of affliction give rise to the eighty-four thousand forms of worldly defilement — hence it should be known that the five gates are likewise able to give rise to eighty-four thousand dharma-gates. Speaking in this way, then, though only five gates are named, every internal wholesomeness is thereby encompassed in full. What the Ābhidharma masters clarify as the five contemplations that still the mind, arising at the initial stage of worthies, has points of overlap with what is given here.

This section pairs neatly with fascicle 2's twenty-five preliminary conditions: those were conditions for practice to even begin; this is a diagnostic for what stopping actually surfaces once it has begun. "External" wholesomeness (giving, precepts, filial devotion, faith, study) is ordinary ethical cultivation done with a still-scattered mind; "internal" wholesomeness is the five-gate dhyāna that already reaches toward uncontaminated attainment. Notice, too, the deliberate correspondence Zhiyi draws to the Ābhidharma tradition's own "five contemplations that still the mind" (五停心觀) — the treatise is not inventing an idiosyncratic scheme so much as mapping its own five gates onto a category practitioners from other lineages would already recognize.

quiz.q: On the verification of stopping, what are the two masters' views?
options: one: stopping has no distinct realization, only serving as a preliminary; the other: it has its own realization, the five-wheel dhyāna
stopping is the four dhyānas; stopping is cessation
both say only ordinary people practice it
quiz.why: "One master says: 'Stopping has no distinct realization of its own — it can only serve as the preliminary expedient means for the other dhyānas.' ... A second master says: 'Stopping not only generally brings forth every dhyāna in common, but also has its own distinct method of realization — namely, the five-wheel dhyāna.'"

quiz.q: What are the five wheels, and why are they called "wheels"?
options: earth, water, fire, wind, space; wheels are round
gold, silver, copper, iron, Dharma wheels
earth, water, wind, golden-sand, vajra; a wheel turns, as the earth wheel turns the scattered mind from the lower to a higher stage
quiz.why: "The five wheels are: the earth wheel; the water wheel; the wind wheel; the golden-sand wheel; and the vajra wheel ... They are called, in general, 'wheels' because a wheel turns ... the earth wheel, for instance, is so named because it turns the scattered mind of the lower stage away and moves it to a higher stage."

quiz.q: Simply by restraining the mind to one place, the five wheels arise of themselves. What simile is used?
options: like clear water without ripples, in which every reflection appears
quiz.why: "This stopping alone, simply by restraining the mind to a single place, brings forth the five wheels of itself — just as, when clear water is free of ripples, the ten thousand reflections all appear within it of themselves."

quiz.q: What two properties does the earth wheel have, and how do they apply in dhyāna?
options: sustaining unmoved: realizing the not-yet-arrived state, concentration sustains the mind; giving birth: from it the merits of the first dhyāna arise
quiz.why: "Earth has two properties — first, sustaining and remaining unmoved; second, giving birth to the ten thousand things ... the dharma of concentration itself then sustains the mind unmoved ... And because the 'not-yet-arrived' state gives rise to the various merits of the first dhyāna, this matches the property of giving birth."

quiz.q: In the water wheel, what do "moistening" and "softness" refer to in dhyāna?
options: severing views and afflictions; three fruits
the water of concentration moistens the mind and wholesome roots grow; body and mind become pliant, arrogance is subdued, and the mind follows the good
quiz.why: "The water of concentration moistens the mind, and one becomes aware of oneself that wholesome roots are growing within the mind — this is the meaning of moistening. And because concentration is attained, body and mind become soft and pliant, arrogance is subdued, and the mind comes to follow wholesome dharmas — this is the meaning of softness."

quiz.q: Among the wind wheel's three properties, what is "destroying," and what stage does it mark for the two vehicles and for bodhisattvas?
options: destroying the body; first fruit; ten grounds

skillful wisdom crushes every wrong view and affliction; for the two vehicles, approximate uncontaminated understanding of the five expedients; for bodhisattvas, the iron wheel of the ten stages of faith
quiz.why: "As for destroying: skillful wisdom is able to crush and destroy every wrong view and affliction. If a follower of the two lesser vehicles attains this samādhi of the wind wheel, this is precisely the arising of an approximate, uncontaminated understanding through the five expedient means. If it is a bodhisattva, this is precisely entering the iron wheel of the ten stages of faith." The three worthies and ten grounds belong to the golden-sand wheel.

quiz.q: In the golden-sand wheel, what do "gold" and "sand" stand for?
options: gold for truth, sand for non-attachment
gold for concentration, sand for scattering
gold for the Buddha, sand for beings
gold for merit, sand for affliction
quiz.why: "The golden-sand wheel: gold here serves as a metaphor for truth, and sand serves as a metaphor for non-attachment. If the practitioner brings forth the true wisdom that severs the views and the discursive afflictions, undefiled and unattached, the fruits of the three lower paths are attained."

options: the ninth unobstructed path, the vajra-wheel samādhi; it severs every fetter and accomplishes arhatship; in a bodhisattva it is vajra-like prajñā, also called the pure-and-undefiled dhyāna
quiz.why: "The vajra wheel: the ninth unobstructed path is called the vajra-wheel samādhi ... it is able to sever every fetter, and thereby accomplishes arhatship. Within a bodhisattva's mind, this is precisely the vajra-like prajñā ... also called the pure-and-undefiled dhyāna."

quiz.q: "A wheel without an ox to drive it will never turn on its own" — what does this illustrate?
options: without embodying-truth stopping as guide and cultivation free of attachment, obstruction arises at every stage and the wheels fail
quiz.why: "Just as a wheel, without an ox to drive it, will never turn on its own, the dhyāna-concentration of the five wheels is exactly the same ... if embodying-truth stopping is not taken as the guide, and cultivation is not carried out free of attachment, then obstruction arises at every single stage, and the wheel's own function fails."

quiz.q: Which Lotus Sūtra line closes the discussion of the five wheels?
options: there is only the one vehicle
dharmas from the beginning are ever quiescent
beings are attached everywhere; the Buddha leads them out
quiz.why: "Hence the Lotus Sūtra says: 'Sentient beings are attached everywhere they turn; the Buddha leads them so that they may find their way out.' One should know, then, that a practitioner who skillfully cultivates the gate of stopping is thereby able to be complete in the dhyāna-concentration of the five wheels."

quiz.q: Why must wholesome and unwholesome capacity be verified after cultivating stopping, and what sūtra line is cited?
options: when the mind is still, past wholesome roots arise, or else unwholesome dharmas; "First stir it through concentration, then draw it out through wisdom"
because the unwholesome always arises first
quiz.why: "Because the mind is still, wholesome roots from past lives naturally come to be brought forth of themselves. Where there is nothing wholesome present, unwholesome dharmas are instead brought forth. Hence the sūtra says: 'First stir it through concentration, then draw it out through wisdom.'" The order is not fixed.

quiz.q: Which arises first, the wholesome or the unwholesome?
options: it follows each person; it is not fixed that the wholesome comes first
quiz.why: "As for the actual order in which the wholesome and the unwholesome arise, however, this follows each individual practitioner — it is not necessarily fixed that the wholesome always arises first and the unwholesome only afterward."

quiz.q: Verifying wholesome capacity has four parts. Which?
options: listing the topics, the marks of arising, verifying genuine or false, the unfixed arising of dhyāna
quiz.why: "Clarifying how to verify wholesome capacity: this itself has four parts — first, listing the topics of the wholesome dharmas; second, directly clarifying the marks of wholesome roots arising; third, verifying whether they are genuine or false; fourth, distinguishing that the arising of dhyāna through this is not fixed."

quiz.q: Which correctly lists the five kinds of external wholesomeness?
options: giving, precepts, filial devotion to parents and teachers, faith in the Triple Gem with offering, reading and study
quiz.why: "In brief, five kinds are given: giving; upholding the precepts; filial devotion to parents and teachers; faith and reverence toward the Triple Gem, together with diligent offering; and reading, reciting, and studying the teachings." The five gates beginning with the breath are internal wholesomeness.

quiz.q: Why are these five all classed as external wholesomeness?
options: their original practice was cultivated with a scattered mind, unable to leave the desire realm or bring forth dhyāna and the uncontaminated
because they are outside the body
because they are done for others
quiz.why: "The reason all five are classed as external wholesomeness is that their original practice is, in every case, cultivated within a scattered mind, not yet able to leave the desire realm behind."

quiz.q: Internal wholesomeness is which five-gate dhyāna?
options: the breath, impurity, loving-kindness, causation, buddha-recollection samādhi
quiz.why: "Internal wholesomeness: this is precisely the five-gate dhyāna — the gate of mindfulness of the breath; the gate of the contemplation of impurity; the gate of loving-kindness; the gate of causation; and the gate of the buddha-recollection samādhi."

quiz.q: To which dhyānas does the gate of buddha-recollection extend?
options: the root dhyānas, special excellences, thorough-and-bright
the nine kinds of dhyāna and the one hundred eight samādhis
quiz.why: "The gate of buddha-recollection extends all the way to the nine kinds of great dhyāna and the one hundred eight samādhis." The root dhyānas belong to the breath, the nine contemplations to impurity, and the immeasurables to loving-kindness.

quiz.q: In the shallow-to-deep order of the five gates, who cultivates the gate of loving-kindness?
options: both ordinary people and the noble, for great merit, entering the four immeasurables
quiz.why: "Next, the gate of loving-kindness is precisely what both ordinary people and the noble cultivate together, for the sake of great merit, entering the four immeasurable minds." Counting the breath is the ordinary person's, impurity the śrāvaka's, causation the pratyekabuddha's, and buddha-recollection the bodhisattva's.
